question: Since 2011 the supreme court banned the manufacture, sale and use of which pesticide that cause hazardous effects to human life as well as the environment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Malathion
Endosulfan
Clothianidin
Chlorpyrifos
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Endosulfan

Explanation:
Endosulfan is a highly toxic organochlorine insecticide that was banned by the Supreme Court of India in 2011. It poses serious risks to human health and the environment, including neurotoxicity, reproductive disorders, and endocrine disruption. The Court imposed a complete ban on its manufacture, sale, and use because it persists in soil, water, and air for long periods. Other options like Malathion and Chlorpyrifos are also hazardous but not completely banned. Clothianidin is a neonicotinoid harmful to bees.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Insecticide banned by Supreme Court in 2011 → Endosulfan
☛ Chemical class of Endosulfan → Organochlorine
☛ Health effects of Endosulfan → Neurotoxic, reproductive issues
☛ Crops where Endosulfan was used → Cotton, tea, vegetables
☛ International status of Endosulfan → Listed as POP under Stockholm Convention

question: As per the Constitution of India, every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of ______ hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: 10
36
24
12
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 24

Explanation:
According to Article 22 of the Constitution of India, every person arrested and detained must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, excluding the time required for the journey from the place of arrest to the court. This provision is a fundamental right designed to protect individuals from arbitrary detention and ensure judicial oversight. It prevents police from holding a person unlawfully and provides the accused with an opportunity for judicial review. This safeguard is crucial in a democratic society to prevent abuse of power and uphold the rule of law.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Time limit to produce arrested person before magistrate → 24 hours
☛ Article that provides this protection → Article 22
☛ Is travel time included in the 24 hours? → No
☛ Which part of Constitution contains this right? → Fundamental Rights
☛ Article 22 deals with → Protection against arrest and detention
question_hi: भारत के संविधान के अनुसार, गिरफ्तार किए गए और हिरासत में लिए गए प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को गिरफ्तारी के ______ घंटे की अवधि के भीतर निकटतम मजिस्ट्रेट के समक्ष पेश किया जाएगा, जिसमें गिरफ्तारी के स्थान से मजिस्ट्रेट की न्यायालय तक की यात्रा के लिए आवश्यक समय शामिल नहीं है। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The United Nations (UN) has six language official languages.
The term of a judge in the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is five years.
The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has five permanent members.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has fifteen judges.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The term of a judge in the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is five years.

Explanation:
This statement is incorrect because the term of a judge in the ICJ is nine years, not five. The United Nations has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish. The UNSC has five permanent members: the US, UK, France, Russia, and China. The ICJ consists of fifteen judges, elected by the General Assembly and the Security Council. Their term is nine years and they are eligible for re-election. Thus, only the second option is wrong.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ ICJ judges' term → 9 years
☛ UN official languages → 6
☛ UNSC permanent members → 5
☛ Total ICJ judges → 15
☛ ICJ headquarters → The Hague, Netherlands

Explanation:
यह कथन गलत है क्योंकि ICJ में न्यायाधीशों का कार्यकाल नौ वर्ष का होता है, पाँच वर्ष का नहीं। संयुक्त राष्ट्र की छह आधिकारिक भाषाएँ हैं: अरबी, चीनी, अंग्रेजी, फ्रेंच, रूसी और स्पेनिश। UNSC के पाँच स्थायी सदस्य हैं: अमेरिका, ब्रिटेन, फ्रांस, रूस और चीन। ICJ में पंद्रह न्यायाधीश होते हैं, जिन्हें महासभा और सुरक्षा परिषद द्वारा चुना जाता है। न्यायाधीशों का कार्यकाल नौ वर्ष का होता है और वे पुनः चुने जा सकते हैं। इस प्रकार, केवल दूसरा विकल्प गलत है।

question: Which of the following statement is correct? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: The Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.
The Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the Vice-President.
The Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Council of the State.
The Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the Council of States.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers in a state is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state. This provision is based on the parliamentary system, where the executive is accountable to the legislature. If the council loses the majority in the Assembly, it must resign. The other options are incorrect because the council is not responsible to the Vice-President, the Legislative Council, or the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Collective responsibility of state cabinet → Enshrined in Article 164
☛ State cabinet is responsible to → State Legislative Assembly
☛ In parliamentary system, executive → Accountable to legislature
☛ Tenure of state cabinet → As long as it enjoys confidence of Assembly
☛ Appointment of Chief Minister → By the Governor

question: In the Constitution of India, principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were borrowed from: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: the United States Constitution
the French Constitution
the British Constitution
the Irish Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the French Constitution

Explanation:
The principles of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the French Constitution. These ideals, originating from the French Revolution (1789), are enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. They reflect the commitment to a just and egalitarian society, influencing Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy. The framers adopted these principles to promote individual freedoms, social equality, and national unity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ When did the French Revolution take place? → 1789
☛ Which part of the Indian Constitution mentions these principles? → Preamble
☛ Who called the Preamble the 'soul of the Constitution'? → Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Which document in France first proclaimed these ideals? → Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

question: When is the Constitution Day celebrated in India?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: 26th November
24th January
15th August
26th January
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26 November

Explanation:
In India, Constitution Day is celebrated annually on 26 November. On this day in 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution. However, the Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day. The observance of Constitution Day began in 2015, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced it on the occasion of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's birth anniversary. This day honors the contribution of Dr. Ambedkar in drafting the Constitution. The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Constitution Day → 26 November
☛ Date of adoption of Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ Date of enactment of Constitution → 26 January 1950
☛ Constitution Day started → 2015
☛ Dr. B.R. Ambedkar birth anniversary → 14 April
question_hi: भारत में संविधान दिवस कब मनाया जाता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 1)

24th जनवरी
15th अगस्त

Explanation:
भारत में संविधान दिवस प्रतिवर्ष 26 नवंबर को मनाया जाता है। इस दिन 1949 में भारतीय संविधान सभा द्वारा संविधान को अंगीकृत किया गया था। हालांकि, संविधान 26 जनवरी 1950 को लागू हुआ, जिसे गणतंत्र दिवस के रूप में मनाया जाता है। संविधान दिवस को 2015 से मनाने की शुरुआत हुई, जब प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर की जयंती पर इसकी घोषणा की। यह दिन संविधान निर्माण में डॉ. अंबेडकर के योगदान को सम्मानित करने के लिए भी मनाया जाता है।

question: The concept of ‘directive principles’ in Indian Constitution has been taken from: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Canada

Ireland
Great Britain
solution:

Explanation:
The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution is derived from the Constitution of Ireland. These principles are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution. They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they serve as guidelines for the state in policy-making. The DPSPs aim to establish a welfare state by ensuring social, economic, and political justice. They include Gandhian principles like promotion of cottage industries, prohibition of intoxicating drinks, and organization of village panchayats.

question: In India, impeachment process is NOT applicable to _____ for removal from office. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Chief Justice of India
President of India
Supreme Court Judge
the Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the Prime Minister

Explanation:
In India, the impeachment process is applicable only to the President, Vice President, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and the Chief Election Commissioner. The Prime Minister is an elected member of Parliament and can be removed not by impeachment but by a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha. Impeachment is a judicial process for removal on grounds of violation of the Constitution. The Prime Minister's tenure depends on the majority support in Lok Sabha. Hence, the impeachment process is not applicable to the Prime Minister.

question: What is a mandamus writ? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Calling for an end to hearings
Making a government body do its duty
Coming to an agreement
Producing the person in court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Making a government body do its duty

Explanation:
A mandamus writ is a type of writ that orders a public authority or lower court to perform its public duty. It is issued by High Courts under Article 226 and the Supreme Court under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution. This writ is only granted when no alternative remedy exists and the failure to perform duty violates fundamental rights. The purpose of mandamus is to ensure accountability in administrative actions. It cannot be issued against private individuals, only against public authorities.

question: According to Article 348(1) of the Constitution, which of the following languages are used for proceedings in the High Courts of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
The 91st Amendment to the Indian Constitution inserted the provision in Article 75 that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. question: What do you mean by a specific majority?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Only the majority of half members of the upper house
More than 50 percent of the total members of the House and majority of two-thirds of current members present and voting
Majority of two-thirds members of the House
Less than two thirds majority of present members and voting
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is More than 50 percent of the total members of the House and majority of two-thirds of current members present and voting

Explanation:
In the Indian Constitution, specific majority means that for a motion to be passed, two conditions must be met: first, more than 50% of the total members of the House must be present, and second, a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting must support it. This majority is required for special matters such as constitutional amendments, presidential elections, and removal of high court judges. For example, under Article 368, a constitutional amendment requires a specific majority. This ensures that important decisions are made with broad consensus and not merely by a simple majority.

question: If the bill wants to amend the federal provisions of the Constitution, it will need to be approved by _________. (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: the absolute majority of the State Legislative Council
members of the Rajya Sabha only
a third of the state ministers
the general majority of half the members of the State Legislative Council
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the general majority of half the members of the State Legislative Council

Explanation:
Amending the federal provisions of the Constitution requires a special procedure under Article 368. If a bill affects the federal structure, it must be passed by both Houses of Parliament with a special majority and then ratified by at least half of the state legislatures. In the case of a State Legislative Council, ratification requires the general majority of half of its members. This procedure ensures the protection of the federal system.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 368 → Deals with the procedure for constitutional amendments.
☛ Amending federal provisions → Requires ratification by states.
☛ State Legislative Council → Upper house in states with bicameral legislature.
☛ General majority → Majority of members present and voting.
☛ Federal structure → Division of powers between center and states.
question_hi: यदि विधेयक संविधान के संघीय प्रावधानों में संशोधन करना चाहता है, तो उसे _________ द्वारा अनुमोदित किया जाना आवश्यक होगा। (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: राज्य विधान परिषद का पूर्ण बहुमत
केवल राज्य सभा के सदस्य
राज्य मंत्रियों का एक तिहाई
राज्य विधान परिषद के आधे सदस्यों का सामान्य बहुमत
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य विधान परिषद के आधे सदस्यों का सामान्य बहुमत

Explanation:
संविधान के संघीय प्रावधानों में संशोधन के लिए अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत विशेष प्रक्रिया अपनाई जाती है। यदि कोई विधेयक संघीय ढांचे को प्रभावित करता है, तो उसे संसद के दोनों सदनों में विशेष बहुमत से पारित होने के बाद कम से कम आधे राज्यों के विधानमंडलों द्वारा अनुमोदित किया जाना आवश्यक है। राज्य विधान परिषद के मामले में, अनुमोदन के लिए उसके आधे सदस्यों का सामान्य बहुमत आवश्यक होता है। यह प्रक्रिया संघीय व्यवस्था की सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करती है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ अनुच्छेद 368 → संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है।
☛ संघीय प्रावधानों में संशोधन → राज्यों के अनुमोदन की आवश्यकता होती है।
☛ राज्य विधान परिषद → द्विसदनीय विधानमंडल वाले राज्यों में ऊपरी सदन।
☛ सामान्य बहुमत → उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का बहुमत।
☛ संघीय ढांचा → राज्यों और केंद्र के बीच शक्तियों का विभाजन।

question: The provision of appointment of state governors by the national government has been taken from the constitution of which country? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: the Weimar Constitution
the Constitution of Ireland
the Canadian Constitution
the Constitution of Australia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the Canadian Constitution

Explanation:
The provision for appointment of state governors by the national government in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Canadian Constitution. In Canada, the Lieutenant Governors of provinces are appointed by the federal government. This system was adopted in India to maintain coordination between the centre and states. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts as a representative of the centre. The Indian Constitution has taken provisions from many countries, like the parliamentary system from Britain and the Directive Principles of State Policy from Ireland.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Source of Governor appointment → Canadian Constitution
☛ Source of Parliamentary system → Britain
☛ Source of Directive Principles → Ireland
☛ Source of Preamble ideas → USA
☛ Inspiration for Directive Principles → Ireland
question_hi: राष्ट्रीय सरकार द्वारा राज्य के राज्यपालों की नियुक्ति का प्रावधान किस देश के संविधान से लिया गया है? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: वाइमर संविधान
आयरलैंड का संविधान
कनाडा का संविधान
ऑस्ट्रेलिया का संविधान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कनाडा का संविधान

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है, यह प्रावधान कनाडा के संविधान से लिया गया है। कनाडा में प्रांतों के लेफ्टिनेंट गवर्नर की नियुक्ति संघीय सरकार करती है। यह प्रणाली भारत में अपनाई गई ताकि केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच समन्वय बना रहे। राज्यपाल राज्य का संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है और केंद्र के प्रतिनिधि के रूप में कार्य करता है। भारतीय संविधान ने कई देशों के संविधानों से प्रावधान ग्रहण किए हैं, जैसे ब्रिटेन से संसदीय प्रणाली और आयरलैंड से राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ राज्यपाल नियुक्ति का स्रोत → कनाडा का संविधान
☛ संसदीय प्रणाली का स्रोत → ब्रिटेन
☛ राज्य नीति निदेशक सिद्धांत → आयरलैंड
☛ प्रस्तावना के विचार → अमेरिका
☛ नीति निदेशक तत्व प्रेरणा → आयरलैंड
